title: Studying word order through iterative shuffling
abstract: arXiv:2109.04867v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: As neural language models approach human performance on NLP benchmark tasks, their advances are widely seen as evidence of an increasingly complex understanding of syntax. This view rests upon a hypothesis that has not yet been empirically tested: that word order encodes meaning essential to performing these tasks. We refute this hypothesis in many cases: in the GLUE suite and in various genres of English text, the words in a sentence or phrase can rarely be permuted to form a phrase carrying substantially different information. Our surprising result relies on inference by iterative shuffling (IBIS), a novel, efficient procedure that finds the ordering of a bag of words having the highest likelihood under a fixed language model. IBIS can use any black-box model without additional training and is superior to existing word ordering algorithms. translated_title: 通过迭代洗牌研究词序
translated_abstract: 随着神经语言模型在NLP基准任务上的表现接近人类水平，其进步被广泛视为对句法理解日益复杂的证据。这一观点基于一个尚未经过实证检验的假设：词序编码了对执行这些任务至关重要的语义。我们在许多情况下驳斥了这一假设：在GLUE基准套件和各类英文文本体裁中，句子或短语中的词语很少能通过重新排列形成携带实质不同信息的短语。我们这一令人惊讶的结果依赖于迭代洗牌推理（IBIS），这是一种新颖且高效的程序，能够在固定语言模型下找出一组词语具有最高可能性的排序。IBIS可以使用任何黑盒模型而无需额外训练，并且优于现有的词序排序算法。综合我们的研究发现，我们讨论了诸如IBIS之类的洗牌推理程序如何有益于……
tldr: 该论文提出了一种名为IBIS（迭代洗牌推理）的新颖高效算法，能在固定语言模型下找到词语的最优排序，并利用该方法发现句子中的词语很少能被重排成含义截然不同的短语，从而在许多情况下驳斥了“词序编码对NLP任务至关重要的语义”这一假设。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces IBIS (inference by iterative shuffling), a novel efficient procedure for finding the highest-likelihood word ordering under a fixed language model, and uses it to show that words in sentences can rarely be permuted to form phrases carrying substantially different information, refuting the hypothesis that word order encodes meaning essential to NLP benchmark tasks.
